question: Who founded the Chola empire?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vijayalaya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vijayalaya founded the (imperial) Chola dynasty in the 9th century CE, around 850 CE, by capturing Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyars. (चोल साम्राज्य — विजयालय)

 

• He ruled as a feudatory of the Pallavas initially and built a temple to Nishumbhasudini (Durga) at Thanjavur to commemorate his victory.

 

• His successors — Aditya I, Parantaka I, Rajaraja I and Rajendra I — expanded the Chola empire into one of the greatest South Indian empires, with Rajaraja I building the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur.

 

• The imperial Cholas are distinguished from the earlier Sangam-age Cholas, who ruled much earlier and are mentioned in Sangam literature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chola administration is well known for its local self-government, with village assemblies like Ur, Sabha and Nagaram, recorded in inscriptions such as the Uttaramerur inscriptions.

 

• The Cholas had a strong navy and extended their influence to Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia.

 

NOTE

 

• Dantidurga (Option 1): He founded the Rashtrakuta dynasty in the 8th century CE.

 

• Simhavishnu (Option 2): He was the founder-ruler of the Pallava dynasty of Kanchipuram.

 

• Upendra/Upendrarai (Option 3): He is regarded as the founder of the Paramara dynasty of Malwa.

question: Arvind Parikh is associated with which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sitar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Arvind Parikh is a renowned Indian classical sitar player belonging to the Imdadkhani (Etawah) gharana. (सितार वादक — अरविंद पारीख)

 

• He is a leading disciple of the legendary sitarist Ustad Vilayat Khan.

 

• Besides performing, he is known for his contribution to musicology and music education, and has headed institutions like the ITC Sangeet Research Academy.

 

• He has been honoured with several awards for his contribution to Hindustani classical music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Famous sitar players of India include Pandit Ravi Shankar, Ustad Vilayat Khan, and Ustad Shahid Parvez Khan.

 

NOTE

 

• Shehnai (Option 1): Associated with maestros like Ustad Bismillah Khan.

 

• Mridangam (Option 2): A percussion instrument central to Carnatic music, associated with artists like Palghat Mani Iyer.

 

• Tabla (Option 3): Associated with maestros like Ustad Zakir Hussain and Ustad Alla Rakha.

question: India's first and the world's second 100% methanol-powered prototype truck was unveiled in _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bengaluru.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's first and the world's second 100% methanol-powered prototype truck was unveiled in Bengaluru, developed jointly by the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Tata Motors and the Methanol Institute. (मेथनॉल ट्रक — बेंगलुरु)

 

• The initiative supports the government's push for alternative and cleaner fuels under the NITI Aayog-backed Methanol Economy programme, championed by Nitin Gadkari.

 

• Methanol can be produced domestically from coal, natural gas, agricultural residue and municipal solid waste, reducing India's dependence on imported crude oil.

 

• The prototype truck demonstrates the feasibility of methanol as a cleaner substitute for diesel in heavy commercial vehicles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• China was the first country to unveil a 100% methanol-powered prototype truck, making India's Bengaluru truck the world's second.

 

• Bengaluru has also seen the launch of methanol-run buses as part of similar clean-fuel trials.

 

NOTE

 

• Delhi, Hyderabad and Chennai (Options 2, 3, 4): The methanol truck was not unveiled in any of these cities; the launch event was held in Bengaluru.

question: Onam is a state festival of __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Onam is the most important and widely celebrated harvest festival of Kerala, observed in the Malayalam month of Chingam (August-September). (ओणम — केरल)

 

• It commemorates the annual visit of the mythical king Mahabali (Maveli) to his subjects.

 

• It is celebrated with Pookalam (floral rangoli), the grand feast Onasadya, and boat races known as Vallam Kali, including the famous Nehru Trophy Boat Race.

 

• The festival is celebrated by people of Kerala across all religions, reflecting its cultural and secular importance to the state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Aranmula Boat Race and Pulikali (tiger dance) at Thrissur are also associated with Onam celebrations.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat (Option 1): Its notable festivals include Navratri and Kite Festival (Uttarayan).

 

• Karnataka (Option 2): Its state festivals include Ugadi and Mysuru Dasara.

 

• Goa (Option 3): Known for the Goa Carnival and Shigmo festival.

question: Which of the following is NOT an objective of National Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy (2007) of the Government of India?
option_1: To maximise the focus on rehabilitation without really caring for resettlement
option_2: To integrate rehabilitation concerns into the development planning and implementation process
option_3: To minimise displacement and to promote, as far as possible, non-displacing or least-displacing alternatives
option_4: To provide a better standard of living, making concerted efforts for providing sustainable income to the affected families
solution_text:
The correct answer is To maximise the focus on rehabilitation without really caring for resettlement.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy (NRRP), 2007 explicitly aims to give equal and integrated focus to BOTH rehabilitation and resettlement of project-affected families, not one at the cost of the other. (राष्ट्रीय पुनर्वास एवं पुनर्स्थापन नीति 2007 — पुनर्वास व पुनर्स्थापन दोनों पर ध्यान)

 

• The policy specifically seeks to minimise large-scale displacement and to prefer non-displacing or least-displacing alternatives wherever feasible.

 

• It aims to integrate rehabilitation and resettlement concerns into the development planning process, and to ensure a better standard of living with sustainable income opportunities for project-affected families.

 

• The idea of focusing on rehabilitation without caring for resettlement runs contrary to the policy's core principle of holistic, balanced attention to both aspects.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• NRRP 2007 was later substantially replaced by the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (RFCTLARR) Act, 2013.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2: This is a genuine objective — integrating R&R concerns into development planning is a core aim of the 2007 policy.

 

• Option 3: This is a genuine objective — minimising displacement and preferring least-displacing alternatives is explicitly stated in the policy.

 

• Option 4: This is a genuine objective — providing a better, sustainable standard of living to affected families is a stated goal of the policy.

question: What is the purpose of the Earth's magnetic field?
option_1: To provide an energy source for life on Earth
option_3: To shield the Earth from solar wind and cosmic radiation
option_4: To cause the tides in the ocean
solution_text:
The correct answer is To shield the Earth from solar wind and cosmic radiation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Earth's magnetic field, generated by the geodynamo effect in the outer core, forms the magnetosphere, which deflects charged particles from the solar wind and harmful cosmic radiation. (पृथ्वी का चुंबकीय क्षेत्र — सौर वायु से सुरक्षा)

 

• Without this protective shield, solar wind would strip away the atmosphere over time, as is believed to have happened on Mars.

 

• The interaction of solar wind particles with the magnetosphere near the poles produces the auroras (Aurora Borealis and Aurora Australis).

 

• The magnetic field also enables navigation using a compass, as it aligns with roughly the geographic North-South axis.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Earth's magnetic poles are not fixed and undergo secular variation, and have even reversed polarity in geological history.

 

• The Van Allen radiation belts are regions of trapped charged particles held by the Earth's magnetic field.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: The Earth's magnetic field does not provide energy; the Sun is the primary energy source for life on Earth.

 

• Option 2: Climate is primarily controlled by solar radiation, the atmosphere, and ocean currents, not the magnetic field.

 

• Option 4: Ocean tides are caused by the gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun, not the Earth's magnetic field.

question: Which mineral salt is dissolved in major amount in ocean water?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sodium chloride.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sodium chloride (NaCl), common salt, makes up about 77-78% of the total dissolved salts in ocean/sea water, making it the most abundant dissolved mineral salt. (सोडियम क्लोराइड — समुद्री जल का प्रमुख लवण)

 

• The average salinity of ocean water is about 35 parts per thousand (‰), meaning roughly 35 grams of dissolved salts per litre of seawater.

 

• Other salts present in smaller quantities include magnesium chloride, magnesium sulphate, calcium sulphate and potassium sulphate.

 

• Salinity varies with evaporation, precipitation, river inflow, and ice formation/melting across different ocean regions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Dead Sea and the Great Salt Lake have far higher salinity than the open ocean due to high evaporation and no outlet.

 

• The Red Sea is one of the most saline open seas due to high evaporation and low freshwater inflow.

 

NOTE

 

• Calcium chloride (Option 1): Present in seawater only in minor amounts, not the dominant dissolved salt.

 

• Calcium carbonate (Option 2): Present in much smaller quantities; it is important for marine shell/skeleton formation, not the majority dissolved salt.

 

• Calcium sulphate (Option 4): Present in seawater only in minor amounts compared to sodium chloride.

question: X and Y are working as managers in a restaurant but they receive unequal pay for the same work. Which Article of the Directive Principles of State Policy provides for equal pay for equal work?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 39.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 39(d) of the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV) directs the State to ensure equal pay for equal work for both men and women. (समान कार्य के लिए समान वेतन — अनुच्छेद 39)

 

• Article 39 as a whole lays down several principles of policy, including adequate means of livelihood, equitable distribution of material resources, and prevention of concentration of wealth.

 

• Since X and Y perform the same work (managers) but receive unequal pay, this directly falls under the equal-pay-for-equal-work principle enshrined in Article 39(d).

 

• The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 was enacted to give statutory effect to this directive principle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Supreme Court, in cases like Randhir Singh v. Union of India (1982), has read the principle of equal pay for equal work into Article 14 (equality) and Article 16 as well, making it enforceable.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 38 (Option 1): Directs the State to promote the welfare of the people by securing a social order permeated by justice.

 

• Article 41 (Option 2): Provides for the right to work, education and public assistance in certain cases like unemployment, old age and sickness.

 

• Article 40 (Option 4): Directs the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government.

question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of National Highways in India?
option_2: Connect state capitals and major cities
option_3: Construction of border roads in high altitude areas
solution_text:
The correct answer is Construction of border roads in high altitude areas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• National Highways are the primary road network connecting state capitals, major cities, ports and industrial centres, and facilitate inter-state and international transport. (राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग — केंद्र सरकार द्वारा रखरखाव)

 

• They are constructed and maintained by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, i.e., a Central Government responsibility.

 

• Construction of strategic roads in high-altitude border areas is primarily the responsibility of the Border Roads Organisation (BRO), under the Ministry of Defence, not a defining function of National Highways in general.

 

• While some National Highways do pass through border regions, building roads specifically for border/high-altitude strategic purposes is not what characterises National Highways as a category.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has one of the largest road networks in the world; National Highways form a small percentage of total road length but carry a large share of road traffic.

 

• State Highways connect major cities within a state and link with National Highways, while District Roads serve rural connectivity.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Being meant for inter-state transport is a genuine characteristic of National Highways.

 

• Option 2: Connecting state capitals and major cities is a genuine characteristic of National Highways.

 

• Option 4: National Highways are indeed maintained by the Central Government (via NHAI), a genuine characteristic.

question: The Government Budget is a statement of estimates of the government receipts and government expenditure for the coming financial year. The financial year for India is the period from ______ to ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is April 1 to March 31.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's financial year (fiscal year) runs from 1 April to 31 March of the following calendar year. (वित्तीय वर्ष — 1 अप्रैल से 31 मार्च)

 

• The Union Budget is presented by the Finance Minister, conventionally on 1 February, for the upcoming financial year starting 1 April.

 

• The Union Budget is prepared and presented under Article 112 of the Constitution, referred to as the Annual Financial Statement.

 

• This April-March cycle is followed for accounting, taxation (Income Tax) and government budgeting purposes in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A committee headed by Shankar Acharya examined the idea of shifting India's financial year to January-December but the change has not been implemented.

 

• The practice of presenting the Budget on 1 February (instead of the earlier last-day-of-February convention) was introduced from 2017.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3: None of these represent India's actual financial year cycle, which runs from 1 April to 31 March.

question: Which part of a cell converts nutrients into energy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mitochondria.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mitochondria are membrane-bound organelles often called the "powerhouse of the cell" because they convert nutrients into usable energy in the form of ATP (adenosine triphosphate) through cellular/aerobic respiration. (माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया — कोशिका का पावरहाउस)

 

• Mitochondria have their own DNA and double membrane structure (outer and inner membrane, the inner one folded into cristae), and are believed to have originated from ancient bacteria (endosymbiotic theory).

 

• The energy released is used to power almost all cellular activities, including muscle contraction, protein synthesis and active transport.

 

• Cells with high energy demand, such as muscle cells and liver cells, contain a large number of mitochondria.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The nucleus, not listed here, is the control centre of the cell and houses the genetic material.

 

• Chloroplasts (in plant cells) similarly convert light energy into chemical energy through photosynthesis.

 

NOTE

 

• Cell membrane (Option 1): Regulates the movement of substances into and out of the cell; does not generate energy.

 

• Lysosomes (Option 2): Known as the "suicide bags" of the cell, they contain digestive enzymes for breaking down waste material, not for energy conversion.

 

• Chromosome (Option 4): Carries genetic material (DNA) and is involved in heredity, not energy conversion.

question: At the Sportster East Sports Conclave 2023, which Indian women's cricket player received the Emerging Hero award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Titas Sadhu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Titas Sadhu, the young Indian women's cricket fast bowler from Bengal, was honoured with the "Emerging Hero" award at the Sportstar Aces Awards 2023. (टिटास साधु — इमर्जिंग हीरो अवार्ड)

 

• She had earlier impressed with her performances for India in the U-19 Women's T20 World Cup 2023, where India won the title, and made her senior international debut in 2023.

 

• The Sportstar Aces Awards, organised by *The Hindu's* sports magazine *Sportstar*, recognise excellence across various sports in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India won the inaugural ICC Women's U19 T20 World Cup 2023 held in South Africa, with Shafali Verma as captain.

 

• Other prominent young pacers who have emerged in Indian women's cricket alongside Titas Sadhu include Renuka Singh Thakur.

 

NOTE

 

• Richa Ghosh (Option 1): A wicketkeeper-batter for India, not the recipient of this particular award.

 

• Harleen Deol (Option 2): A middle-order batter and fielder for India, not the recipient of this award.

 

• Deepti Sharma (Option 3): An established India all-rounder, not eligible for the "Emerging" category award.

question: Which of the following schemes aims to provide an integrated property validation solution for rural India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is SVAMITVA.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• SVAMITVA (Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas) scheme, launched on 24 April 2020 (National Panchayati Raj Day), provides an integrated property validation solution for rural India using drone survey technology. (स्वामित्व योजना — ग्रामीण संपत्ति सत्यापन)

 

• It is implemented by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, with technical support from the Survey of India, to issue Property Cards (Rights Records) to rural households.

 

• The scheme aims to bring clarity on property rights, reduce property-related disputes, enable rural residents to use property as a financial asset for loans, and support accurate land records.

 

• Drone-based mapping under SVAMITVA creates large-scale maps of rural residential (abadi) areas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• SVAMITVA falls under the broader Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP) framework.

 

NOTE

 

• WDF (Option 1): The Warehousing Development Fund, related to warehousing infrastructure, not property validation.

 

• NRLM (Option 3): The National Rural Livelihood Mission, aimed at poverty alleviation through self-help groups, not property validation.

 

• PIDF (Option 4): The Payments Infrastructure Development Fund by RBI, aimed at expanding digital payment acceptance infrastructure, not property validation.

question: What is the monomer unit of glycogen?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Glucose.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Glycogen is a highly branched polysaccharide made up of repeating units of glucose, joined by α-1,4 glycosidic bonds in the chain and α-1,6 glycosidic bonds at branch points. (ग्लाइकोजन — ग्लूकोज का बहुलक)

 

• It serves as the primary storage form of energy/carbohydrate in animals, stored mainly in the liver and muscle cells.

 

• When the body needs energy, glycogen is broken down into glucose through glycogenolysis, releasing glucose into the bloodstream.

 

• Its plant equivalent for energy storage is starch, which is also a polymer of glucose but less branched.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cellulose, the structural polysaccharide in plant cell walls, is also a polymer of glucose but linked by β-1,4 glycosidic bonds.

 

• Excess dietary glucose is converted into glycogen through the process of glycogenesis.

 

NOTE

 

• Fructose (Option 1): A monosaccharide found in fruits and honey; not the monomer of glycogen.

 

• Galactose (Option 3): A monosaccharide that combines with glucose to form lactose; not the monomer of glycogen.

 

• Mannose (Option 4): A monosaccharide involved in glycoprotein synthesis; not the monomer of glycogen.

question:
Which of these statements is INCORRECT about Human Development Index?

1. The level of education is represented in the HDI.

2. It uses the per capita GDP of a country on purchasing power parity terms to represent the income component.

3. Birth rate and death rate are important components of the HDI.

4. Life expectancy at birth is one of the components of the HDI.
option_1: The level of education is represented in the HDI.
option_2: It uses the per capita GDP of a country on purchasing power parity terms to represent the income component.
option_3: Birth rate and death rate are important components of the HDI.
option_4: Life expectancy at birth is one of the components of the HDI.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Birth rate and death rate are important components of the HDI.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Human Development Index (HDI), developed by economists Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen for the UNDP, is a composite index built from exactly three dimensions: health, education and standard of living. (मानव विकास सूचकांक — जन्म व मृत्यु दर शामिल नहीं)

 

• The health dimension is measured by life expectancy at birth, the education dimension by mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling, and the standard-of-living dimension by Gross National Income (GNI) per capita (PPP $).

 

• Birth rate and death rate are demographic indicators used in measures like the population growth rate, but they are not part of the HDI's formula, making this statement incorrect.

 

• Since the question asks for the INCORRECT statement, and Statement 3 wrongly attributes birth/death rate to HDI, it is the answer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's HDI rank has generally placed it in the medium human development category in UNDP's Human Development Reports.

 

• The HDI was first introduced in the Human Development Report of 1990.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Correct statement — the education dimension (level of education/schooling) is indeed represented in the HDI.

 

• Option 2: Broadly correct in intent — income/standard of living is represented using per-capita national income on a PPP basis (technically GNI rather than GDP), consistent with HDI's income component.

 

• Option 4: Correct statement — life expectancy at birth is indeed the indicator for the health dimension of the HDI.

question: Which of the following noble ideals is mentioned in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
option_1: Liberty of expression, civil, political, worship and belief
option_2: Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship
option_3: Liberty of belief, fiscal, personal, faith and worship
option_4: Liberty of opportunity, economic, social, faith and expression
solution_text:
The correct answer is Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Preamble to the Indian Constitution secures to all citizens "LIBERTY of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship" — the exact phrase used in the Constitution. (उद्देशिका — विचार, अभिव्यक्ति, विश्वास, धर्म और उपासना की स्वतंत्रता)

 

• The Preamble also secures JUSTICE (social, economic and political), EQUALITY (of status and of opportunity), and promotes FRATERNITY assuring dignity and unity/integrity of the nation.

 

• These ideals reflect the influence of the French Revolution (Liberty, Equality, Fraternity) and the Objectives Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in the Constituent Assembly.

 

• The Preamble was amended by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, adding the words "Socialist", "Secular" and "Integrity".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Preamble declares India to be a "SOVEREIGN, SOCIALIST, SECULAR, DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC".

 

• The Preamble was described by Justice K.M. Munshi as the "political horoscope" of the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4: Each of these lists a mixture of terms not matching the exact constitutional phrase; only Option 2 correctly reproduces the words used in the Preamble: "thought, expression, belief, faith and worship".

question: In which language was the work of Raja Ram Mohan Roy, 'Gift to Monotheists' originally written?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Persian.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy's work 'Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhiddin' (Gift to Monotheists), published in 1803/1804, was originally written in Persian, with a preface in Arabic. (तोहफत-उल-मुवाहिद्दीन — फारसी भाषा)

 

• In this work, he argued rationally against idol worship and religious superstition, advocating monotheism.

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy, known as the "Father of the Indian Renaissance/Modern India", founded the Brahmo Sabha in 1828, later known as the Brahmo Samaj.

 

• He was proficient in multiple languages including Persian, Arabic, Sanskrit, English, Bengali, Greek and Hebrew, which shaped his comparative religious writings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy played a key role in the abolition of Sati through the Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829 under Governor-General Lord William Bentinck.

 

• He also campaigned for women's rights, English education, and freedom of the press in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Arabic (Option 1): Used only for the preface of the work, not the main text.

 

• Bengali (Option 3): Not the language of this particular work, though Roy wrote extensively in Bengali elsewhere.

 

• Sanskrit (Option 4): Not the language of this particular work; Roy did use Sanskrit scriptures to build his arguments in other writings.

question: According to Census of India 2011, what is the decadal population growth rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 17.7%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, India's decadal (2001-2011) population growth rate was 17.7%, the lowest inter-censal growth rate recorded since independence up to that point. (जनगणना 2011 — दशकीय वृद्धि दर 17.7%)

 

• India's population as per Census 2011 stood at approximately 121.09 crore (1.21 billion).

 

• The sex ratio as per Census 2011 was 943 females per 1000 males, and the literacy rate was 74.04%.

 

• The 2011 Census was the 15th Census of India and the 7th after independence, conducted under the Census Act, 1948.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Uttar Pradesh was the most populous state as per Census 2011, while Sikkim was the least populous state.

 

• Kerala had the highest literacy rate and sex ratio among major states as per Census 2011.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3: None of these figures (16.2%, 17.2%, 16.7%) match the actual decadal growth rate of 17.7% recorded in Census 2011.

question: With which of the following awards was Kuchipudi dancer V Satyanarayana Sarma honoured?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Shri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma, a renowned Kuchipudi dance exponent famous for his portrayal of female roles (Stree Vesham), was honoured with the Padma Shri by the Government of India. (वेदांतम सत्यनारायण सर्मा — कुचिपुड़ी नृत्य, पद्म श्री)

 

• He belonged to the traditional Kuchipudi village of Andhra Pradesh and was a leading torch-bearer of the classical Kuchipudi dance-drama tradition.

 

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award in India, given for distinguished contribution in various fields including art.

 

• His contribution helped preserve and popularise the traditional Bhamakalapam style of Kuchipudi performance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Kuchipudi exponents include Vempati Chinna Satyam, who is credited with popularising Kuchipudi as a solo dance form and was also honoured with a Padma award.

 

NOTE

 

• Kalidas Samman (Option 1): A prestigious award given by the Madhya Pradesh Government for contributions to art, literature and classical music/dance in general, not the award linked to him in this context.

 

• Kabir Puraskar (Option 2): An award for promoting communal harmony and national integration, unrelated to this dancer.

 

• Moortidevi Award (Option 4): A literary award given by the Bharatiya Jnanpith, unrelated to dance or this personality.

question: Which of the following is the best estimate of the total borrowings by the government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fiscal Deficit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fiscal Deficit is the difference between the government's total expenditure and its total receipts excluding borrowings, and it represents the total borrowing requirement of the government in a financial year. (राजकोषीय घाटा — सरकार की कुल उधारी)

 

• It is calculated as: Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure − (Revenue Receipts + Non-debt Capital Receipts).

 

• A high fiscal deficit indicates that the government needs to borrow more, either domestically or externally, to meet its expenditure needs.

 

• Fiscal deficit is usually expressed as a percentage of GDP and is a key indicator of a government's fiscal health.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit − Interest Payments, indicating the borrowing requirement excluding interest on past debt.

 

• The FRBM Act, 2003 (Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act) sets targets to control India's fiscal deficit.

 

NOTE

 

• Primary Deficit (Option 1): Excludes interest payments, so it does not represent the total borrowing requirement.

 

• Revenue Receipts (Option 2): These are tax and non-tax income of the government, not a measure of borrowing.

 

• Money Supply (Option 3): A monetary indicator of currency and deposits in circulation, unrelated to government borrowing.

question: In which year was the Twenty Point Programme (TPP) launched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1975.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Twenty Point Programme (TPP) was launched in 1975 by the then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, during the period of the Emergency, to alleviate poverty and improve the standard of living of the poor. (बीस सूत्री कार्यक्रम — 1975)

 

• The programme covers areas such as poverty eradication, employment, housing, education, health, and social welfare.

 

• The TPP was restructured in 1982 and again in 1986, and most recently in 2006, to align it with contemporary socio-economic priorities such as the National Common Minimum Programme.

 

• It is monitored jointly by the Central and State Governments with periodic reviews.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 20-Point Programme (2006) currently covers 20 points grouped under poverty, employment, housing, education, health, environment, protection and empowerment of the vulnerable sections.

 

NOTE

 

• 2006 (Option 1): This is the year of the most recent restructuring, not the original launch.

 

• 1986 (Option 3): This is the year of one of the intermediate restructurings, not the original launch.

 

• 1982 (Option 4): This is the year of an earlier restructuring, not the original launch.

question: The number of gold medals won by India at the Tokyo Olympics 2020 is _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is one.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won one gold medal at the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021), won by Neeraj Chopra in the men's javelin throw with a throw of 87.58 m. (टोक्यो ओलंपिक 2020 — नीरज चोपड़ा, स्वर्ण पदक)

 

• This was India's first individual Olympic gold medal in athletics and only the second individual gold medal overall (after Abhinav Bindra in shooting at Beijing 2008).

 

• India's total medal tally at Tokyo 2020 was 7 medals: 1 gold (Neeraj Chopra), 2 silver (Mirabai Chanu - weightlifting, Ravi Kumar Dahiya - wrestling), and 4 bronze (PV Sindhu - badminton, Lovlina Borgohain - boxing, Indian Men's Hockey Team, Bajrang Punia - wrestling).

 

• This was India's best-ever performance at a single edition of the Olympic Games at that time, in terms of total medal count.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Tokyo Olympics 2020 were held from 23 July to 8 August 2021, delayed by one year due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (two, three, four): India won only one gold medal at Tokyo 2020, so these figures are incorrect.

question: Dhimsa folk dance is performed by the tribes of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Araku Valley.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dhimsa is a popular tribal folk dance performed by tribal communities of the Araku Valley region in Andhra Pradesh (Visakhapatnam/Alluri Sitharama Raju district area). (धिम्सा नृत्य — अराकू घाटी, आंध्र प्रदेश)

 

• It is performed by groups of women in a line or circle, accompanied by traditional instruments like the Dappu, Mori and Tudumu.

 

• The dance is typically performed during festivals, weddings and other social/religious occasions of the tribal communities, such as the Kondh, Bagata and Valmiki tribes.

 

• Dhimsa reflects the vibrant tribal culture of the Eastern Ghats region of Andhra Pradesh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Araku Valley is also famous for its coffee plantations and scenic hill terrain, popular as a tourist destination near Visakhapatnam.

 

NOTE

 

• Solan Valley (Option 1): Located in Himachal Pradesh, not associated with the Dhimsa dance.

 

• Ketti Valley (Option 3): Located in the Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu, not associated with the Dhimsa dance.

 

• Parvati Valley (Option 4): Located in Himachal Pradesh (Kullu district), not associated with the Dhimsa dance.

question: In September 2022, Neeraj Chopra becomes the first Indian to win the Diamond League by winning the Diamond League Final 2022 title at Zurich with a throw of __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 88.44 m.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In September 2022, Neeraj Chopra became the first Indian athlete to win the Diamond League title, winning the Diamond League Final 2022 at Zurich, Switzerland with a best throw of 88.44 m. (नीरज चोपड़ा — डायमंड लीग फाइनल 2022, ज्यूरिख)

 

• This victory came in the men's javelin throw event, adding to Neeraj's growing list of achievements after his Tokyo Olympics 2020 gold and World Championships 2022 silver.

 

• The Diamond League is an annual series of elite track-and-field meetings, and winning it (the Diamond League Trophy) is considered one of the sport's top honours outside of Olympics/World Championships.

 

• With this win, Neeraj Chopra further cemented his position as one of the best javelin throwers in the world.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Neeraj Chopra's personal best (as of the relevant period) was 89.94 m, achieved at the Stockholm Diamond League 2022.

 

• He later won a gold medal at the World Athletics Championships 2023 in Budapest, becoming the first Indian to win a gold at that event.

 

NOTE

 

• 90.08 m, 97.02 m and 89.08 m (Options 1, 3, 4): None of these are the throw distance with which Neeraj Chopra won the Zurich Diamond League Final 2022; his winning throw there was 88.44 m.

question: Which of the following states receives rainfall during the retreating monsoon?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The retreating (post/north-east) monsoon, occurring during October-December, brings significant rainfall to Tamil Nadu and parts of the southeastern coast of India. (मानसून प्रत्यावर्तन — तमिलनाडु में वर्षा)

 

• As the south-west monsoon withdraws, winds reverse direction, picking up moisture over the Bay of Bengal and bringing rain to the Coromandel Coast (Tamil Nadu, southern Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry).

 

• Tamil Nadu receives the major share of its annual rainfall from this north-east/retreating monsoon rather than the south-west monsoon, unlike most other Indian states.

 

• This period is also associated with the formation of cyclones in the Bay of Bengal, which can cause heavy rainfall in this region.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The south-west monsoon (June-September) is the primary rainy season for most of India, including states like Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Bihar.

 

• The retreating monsoon phase is also called the transition season or post-monsoon season.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 1): Receives most of its rainfall from the south-west monsoon, not the retreating monsoon.

 

• Gujarat (Option 2): Receives most of its rainfall from the south-west monsoon, not the retreating monsoon.

 

• Bihar (Option 3): Receives most of its rainfall from the south-west monsoon, not the retreating monsoon.
